research_desc: Survey and observational datasets containing measures of opinions, attitudes or behavioral intentions regarding refugees and asylum seekers (national or comparative public opinion surveys, panel data, targeted refugee attitude modules).
research_narr: Include datasets that contain items or scales measuring attitudes toward refugees/asylum seekers (e.g., willingness to accept refugees, perceived cultural/economic threat, policy preferences, social distance), contact with refugees, or modules on migration where refugee-specific items are present. Include cross-sectional and longitudinal survey data (national polls, ESS, Eurobarometer, SOEP modules, specialised refugee attitude surveys). Exclude datasets that do not contain any refugee-specific attitude items or only administrative records about asylum applications without attitudinal measures.

research_desc: Datasets containing measures of general life satisfaction or global subjective well‑being (single items or multi‑item scales) from national, cross‑national and panel surveys.
research_narr: Include datasets that provide the standard global life satisfaction items (e.g., 'All things considered, how satisfied are you with your life as a whole?') or validated scales (e.g., SWLS), with accompanying sociodemographic and contextual variables for analysis. Typical sources include SOEP, ESS, WVS, Eurobarometer, and other national surveys. Exclude datasets that only contain domain‑specific satisfaction measures without any global life satisfaction item.

research_desc: Datasets that include measures of general self‑efficacy (e.g., GSES items or equivalent scales) collected in surveys, panels or intervention studies.
research_narr: Include datasets with item‑level or scale scores for general self‑efficacy, longitudinal data tracking change in self‑efficacy, and trials that measure pre/post general self‑efficacy. Provide documentation on scale items and scoring. Exclude datasets containing only domain‑specific self‑efficacy measures without a general self‑efficacy instrument.

research_desc: Datasets containing items or modules that measure antisemitic attitudes, beliefs, incident records or complaint datasets documenting antisemitic events.
research_narr: Include survey data with antisemitism items (stereotypes, social distance, Holocaust denial, conspiracy beliefs), incident databases (police/NGO records of antisemitic crimes), and longitudinal surveys tracking antisemitic attitudes. Include datasets with contextual variables enabling analysis (region, demographics, media exposure). Exclude datasets lacking any antisemitism‑specific measures or those limited to unrelated forms of prejudice without antisemitic indicators.

research_desc: Datasets with labour market and employment information: household and labour force surveys, administrative employment records, panel data and employer surveys.
research_narr: Include datasets containing employment status, occupation and industry codes, hours worked, contract type, earnings/wages, unemployment spells, job search behaviour, and employer-level variables. Typical sources: labor force surveys, SOEP, microcensus, IAB, administrative unemployment records. Exclude datasets without employment-related variables or those purely focused on education without employment linkage.

research_desc: Survey datasets, cohort studies and administrative data that measure work-related stressors, workload, exposures to physical/psychosocial hazards, and related health or absence outcomes.
research_narr: Include datasets containing measures of job demands, job control, effort-reward imbalance, working hours, shift work, ergonomic exposures, sickness absence, mental health indicators, and biomarkers linked to occupational burden. Include longitudinal employer or workforce panels, occupational health surveillance, and national working conditions surveys that enable analysis of exposure-outcome relationships. Exclude datasets that do not contain workplace-specific exposure or outcome variables (e.g. general population health datasets without occupational information) or datasets focused exclusively on non-occupational stressors.

research_desc: Datasets and surveys containing measures of job satisfaction and related employee attitude variables across occupations, sectors, and time.
research_narr: Include workplace surveys, employee panels, national labour force or working conditions surveys, and longitudinal studies that include single-item or multi-item job satisfaction measures and related covariates (e.g. pay, autonomy, working hours). Include employer-level datasets that record employee engagement or satisfaction metrics. Exclude datasets lacking explicit job satisfaction indicators or those focused on non-employee populations.

research_desc: Enterprise- and establishment-level datasets capturing workplace practices, employment structure, working conditions, and company-level outcomes.
research_narr: Include establishment surveys, employer panels, workplace audits, HR administrative records, and matched employer-employee datasets that record management practices, working hours, shift organization, collective bargaining coverage, occupational health interventions, and productivity measures. Include datasets enabling analysis at the firm or plant level. Exclude individual-level surveys without linkage to establishment identifiers or datasets that only report macroeconomic aggregates.

research_desc: Datasets measuring time allocation, work–family conflict, caregiving responsibilities, flexible work arrangements, and related outcomes such as well‑being and family functioning.
research_narr: Include time-use surveys, family and household panels, working conditions surveys with work–life modules, employer datasets on flexible work usage, and longitudinal studies tracking work and family outcomes. Include data capturing childcare arrangements, unpaid caregiving, commuting time, telework frequency, and leave uptake. Exclude datasets lacking indicators that link employment arrangements to family or private life domains.

research_desc: General labour and employment datasets such as labour force surveys, panel studies, occupational statistics, and working conditions surveys that provide data on employment and work characteristics.
research_narr: Include national and international labour force surveys, panel datasets (e.g. labor panels), occupational classifications, employer-employee linked datasets, administrative employment records, and working conditions or occupational health datasets that capture employment status, occupation, industry, wages, and working hours. Exclude datasets without employment-related variables or those focused solely on non-labor domains.

research_desc: Datasets and data collections that capture changes in work and employment over time, including longitudinal panel surveys, repeated cross-sections and registries relevant to occupational transformation.
research_narr: Relevant data: longitudinal panel datasets (e.g. national panels), repeated cross-sectional surveys and time-series that measure employment patterns, job tasks, telework, skill requirements, contract types, occupational mobility, and firm-level restructuring; administrative registers on employment, industry/occupation matrices, and cross-national surveys tracking work conditions over time (e.g. EWCS, SOEP). Include documentation, codebooks and harmonised time-series. Exclude: datasets that only contain unrelated demographic data without variables on work change, single-company datasets with no information about structural change, or raw technical datasets about equipment with no labor-focus.

research_desc: Datasets containing information on occupations, job histories, career development and vocational training suitable for research on work and professions.
research_narr: Relevant data: labour force surveys, occupation-coded microdata (with ISCO or national coding), employment registries, career history panels, vocational training modules, employer surveys capturing occupational structure, and harmonised cross-national datasets. Include metadata and codebooks that enable occupational analysis. Exclude: datasets lacking occupational or job-related variables, or datasets focused exclusively on non-work domains (e.g. purely health or housing surveys) unless they include substantive job information.

research_desc: Datasets containing measures of job or work satisfaction and related work-context variables suitable for analysis of determinants and outcomes of job satisfaction.
research_narr: Relevant data: surveys and panels that include job satisfaction items (e.g. single-item or multi-item scales), workplace surveys, longitudinal datasets tracking satisfaction over time (SOEP, EWCS, ESS modules where applicable), and employer surveys with employee well‑being measures. Include data documentation and scales. Exclude: datasets lacking any job satisfaction or workplace-wellbeing indicators.

research_desc: Datasets that measure various dimensions of working conditions, such as physical exposures, psychosocial factors, schedules, and contract types.
research_narr: Relevant data: workplace and employee surveys (e.g. European Working Conditions Survey), occupational health surveillance data, employer records on work schedules and hazards, panel data with work-condition modules, and administrative inspections data. Include variable documentation, exposure metrics and health outcome linkages. Exclude: datasets without items on work environment, exposures or contractual/temporal conditions.

research_desc: Datasets and administrative registers containing unemployment measures, spells, benefit receipt and job-search behaviour for analysis of labour-market non-employment.
research_narr: Relevant data: labour force surveys with unemployment modules, panel datasets recording employment spells and transitions, unemployment registers and administrative benefit records, job-search surveys and youth transition studies. Include documentation on unemployment definitions, spell start/end dates and linkage to demographic and health data. Exclude: datasets without clear unemployment indicators or that only capture informal non-employment without unemployment measures.

research_desc: Datasets and surveys containing commute-specific measures: travel time, distance, mode, frequency, route, departure/arrival times, and commute-related exposures (noise, pollution).
research_narr: Include travel and mobility surveys, time-use surveys with commute modules, household travel surveys, employer travel plans, GPS/transport sensor datasets, national transport or labour force surveys with commute variables, and longitudinal datasets that track changes in commuting. Exclude datasets lacking explicit measures identifying journeys to/from work (e.g., only general mobility without purpose) or datasets that only record workplace location without travel measures.

research_desc: Datasets and registers that record working-time information: employment surveys, time-use studies, payroll records, employer scheduling data, and longitudinal labour market datasets.
research_narr: Include national labour force surveys, enterprise payroll/administrative time records, working-time modules in social surveys (e.g., EWCS), time-use diaries capturing paid work episodes, and longitudinal panels measuring changes in hours or schedules. Prefer datasets with both contractual and actual hours, plus shift/roster indicators. Exclude datasets that lack explicit working-time measures or only contain aggregated employment counts without hours or schedule detail.

research_desc: Datasets with migration-related variables: population registers, migration surveys, labour force surveys with country-of-birth or citizenship variables, asylum registers, and longitudinal migration panels.
research_narr: Include administrative population registers that record nationality, country of birth and residency status, specialized migration and integration surveys, household surveys with migration modules, labour market datasets that allow comparison by migration status, and health surveys with migrant identifiers. Exclude datasets lacking any marker of migration/foreign origin or those that only capture temporary visitors/tourists without immigrant status.

research_desc: Datasets capturing job demands and work-related burdens: occupational health surveys, workplace assessments, longitudinal panels with psychosocial measures, and administrative sickness/absence records.
research_narr: Include surveys and datasets that measure job demands, control, effort-reward balance, physical exposures, incidence of work-related illness or injury, and absence records. Examples include workplace health monitoring, national working conditions surveys, and cohort studies linking job exposures to health outcomes. Exclude datasets that measure general stress without specifying work as the source.

research_desc: Datasets that allow joint analysis of work characteristics and burden: combined measures of job exposures and health/stress outcomes, employer records linking workload to performance or absence, and panel data tracking both work conditions and burden over time.
research_narr: Include integrated datasets (working conditions surveys with health modules, longitudinal panels with job and health measures, company HR data linking workload and sick leave) that permit analysis of how work relates to burden and vice versa. Exclude datasets that contain only work attributes or only health/burden measures without the ability to link the two at individual or group level.

research_desc: Datasets and survey modules that capture workplace exposures, psychosocial demands, physical/chemical hazards, injury and absenteeism data.
research_narr: Include cohort studies, cross-sectional surveys and administrative data containing measures of workplace burdens (self-reported demands, COPSOQ/JCQ items, occupational exposure records, accident/compensation registers, sick-leave and disability records), workplace monitoring data and occupational cohort follow-ups. Exclude datasets without workplace-specific exposure or outcome variables and laboratory-only stress measurements not tied to real work settings.

research_desc: Datasets that record occupation, job titles, occupational codes, employment histories and related labor market variables.
research_narr: Include census, labor force surveys, longitudinal panels and administrative datasets containing occupation fields (ISCO/SOC codes), industry, employment status, contract type and detailed job histories. Exclude datasets lacking occupation information or those focused exclusively on non-occupational constructs.

research_desc: Datasets combining detailed measures of educational qualification, field of study and occupational outcomes.
research_narr: Include longitudinal and cross-sectional datasets (e.g., labor force panels, education-to-work cohorts, microcensus) that record highest educational level, vocational qualifications, field of study, training history and subsequent occupational codes, earnings and employment status. Exclude datasets lacking either meaningful education or occupation variables.

research_desc: Datasets and survey modules that include measures of job satisfaction and related workplace attitudinal variables.
research_narr: Include large-scale surveys and panel datasets (e.g., national social surveys, European Working Conditions Survey, SOEP, ALLBUS) that contain single-item or multi-item measures of job satisfaction and facet-specific satisfaction (pay, tasks, colleagues). Exclude datasets without job satisfaction or without identifiable workplace context for satisfaction measures.

research_desc: Datasets containing employment activity measures, task-level job information, work hours and employment spell histories.
research_narr: Include labor force surveys, employment registers, time-use surveys and panel data with variables on employment status, hours worked, job tasks, occupational codes, and employment spells. Include job exposure matrices and datasets with task-based measures. Exclude datasets that do not record actual work activity or that only contain high-level employment indicators without activity detail.

research_desc: Datasets capturing employment histories, job transitions, promotions, occupational codes and timing of job changes (longitudinal or retrospective life-history data), employer/sector information and related socio-demographic variables.
research_narr: Relevant datasets include panel or retrospective surveys and administrative records that record sequences of jobs, dates of job start/stop, occupational codes (e.g., ISCO), job status (employee/self-employed), tenure, promotions, wages, reasons for leaving/entering jobs, and geographic moves for work. Include data enabling analysis of vertical/horizontal mobility and career trajectories. Exclude datasets limited to cross-sectional snapshots without any employment history or datasets about firms rather than individuals, and datasets where job-change information is incidental or unavailable.

research_desc: Survey and panel data containing measures of occupational attitudes and work-related values, including items on job preferences, work ethic, career aspirations and evaluations of occupational roles.
research_narr: Relevant datasets provide attitudinal items (Likert scales or categorical responses) on work values, importance of career success, preference for work–life balance, attitudes toward vocational education, occupational prestige perceptions, and measures of job satisfaction as an attitude. Include longitudinal surveys tracking changes in work attitudes. Exclude datasets with no attitudinal content or those limited to objective employment facts without respondents' opinions or values.

research_desc: Datasets measuring professional identity constructs: occupational self-concept, occupational self-efficacy, career identity, role centrality, and related measures collected in surveys, career studies and longitudinal panels.
research_narr: Relevant datasets contain validated scales or items assessing occupational self-efficacy, strength/centrality of professional identity, identification with occupational groups, perceived competence, and career self-concept measures, including repeated measures over time. Exclude datasets without individual-level psychological measures of occupational self or those focusing only on employer-side organizational identity.

research_desc: Survey data and opinion polls that record evaluations of social policy measures, citizen satisfaction with welfare services, and support for policy instruments and reforms.
research_narr: Relevant datasets feature items on support for welfare spending, satisfaction with specific social programs (pensions, unemployment insurance, health care), perceived effectiveness and fairness of social policy, trust in social institutions, and reactions to policy changes. Include cross-sectional and panel surveys (national and comparative). Exclude datasets that only record policy parameters (benefit levels) without public opinion indicators, or administrative policy implementation data without evaluative measures.

research_desc: Datasets from workplace and organizational surveys that include measures of supervisor–employee relationship quality, supervisory behavior, feedback frequency, mentoring, conflict and trust in direct supervisors.
research_narr: Relevant datasets contain items measuring LMX quality, perceived supervisor support, frequency/quality of feedback, conflict with manager, supervisory fairness, and mentoring experiences, ideally linked to employee outcomes. Include multi-level or matched supervisor–employee surveys. Exclude datasets lacking any supervisor-related attitudinal items or those that record only aggregate leadership ratings without dyadic detail.

research_desc: Datasets and study data on adult education participation, lifelong learning activities, vocational training for adults, continuing education programs, and adult learning outcomes (national surveys, cohort studies, administrative data).
research_narr: Include national or international surveys and administrative datasets that measure adult education participation and training (e.g., Adult Education Survey (AES), PIAAC, CVTS, national continuing education registries), program evaluation datasets, longitudinal studies tracking adult learners, and time-use or labor market linkage data that capture participation in adult learning. Exclude datasets that only cover compulsory school-age children, university students below typical adult-learner contexts, or purely qualitative single-case narratives without structured data unless part of mixed-methods study with extractable data.

research_desc: Datasets and administrative records on paid and unpaid care work, time-use data, labor statistics for care sectors, caregiver surveys, and program evaluations of care services.
research_narr: Include time-use surveys (e.g., national time-use surveys, Eurostat), labor force data for health and social care occupations, caregiver modules in household surveys, longitudinal caregiver panels, datasets on wages/working hours in care professions, and administrative registries for care service provision. Also include datasets capturing informal caregiving prevalence and intensity. Exclude datasets unrelated to caregiving tasks (e.g., general industry data without care-sector detail) or clinical datasets focused only on patient health outcomes without caregiver measures.

research_desc: Survey datasets and opinion polls measuring individual and collective attitudes toward climate change, risk perception, policy preferences, behavioral intentions, and segmentation (e.g., 'Six Americas').
research_narr: Include large cross-national and national surveys with climate attitude modules (e.g., ESS modules when relevant, Eurobarometer, World Values Survey, Gallup, Pew Research, Yale/George Mason 'Climate Change in the American Mind', national climate opinion polls), panel datasets tracking attitude change, and experimental survey data on messaging effects. Exclude purely physical climate datasets (temperature, emissions) unless paired with social opinion measures; exclude datasets without explicit climate-attitude variables.

research_desc: Datasets on climate variables (temperature, precipitation, emissions), impact data (sea-level, crop yields), socio-economic datasets linked to climate (vulnerability, emissions inventories), and integrated datasets combining physical and social indicators.
research_narr: Include observational climate datasets (HadCRUT, CRU, NOAA, NASA GISS), greenhouse gas emissions inventories, CMIP model outputs, impact datasets (sea-level, extreme events), and socio-economic datasets used in climate impact research (agricultural yields, health outcomes, migration linked to climate), as well as integrated assessment model outputs. Exclude datasets that are purely administrative and unrelated to climate or datasets lacking metadata to establish relevance to climate change research.

research_desc: Datasets capturing public attitudes toward democracy, definitions of democracy, evaluations of democratic performance, civic engagement measures, and experimental data on conceptions of democracy (e.g., WVS, ESS, LAPOP).
research_narr: Include cross-national and national surveys with items on support for democracy, definitions (e.g., agreement with democratic statements), preferences for democratic principles (freedom, equality, rule of law), evaluations of democratic performance, and datasets that explore correlates of democratic conceptions (education, political ideology). Also include panel or experimental datasets that probe causal factors shaping conceptions. Exclude datasets that only measure institutional indicators (e.g., V-Dem) without citizen-level conception items, unless combined with public-opinion modules.

research_desc: Datasets capturing consumer choices, intentions and behaviors from surveys, experiments, transaction logs, and observational studies.
research_narr: Include consumer panel and scanner data, household expenditure surveys, online transaction logs, stated-preference and choice-experiment datasets, experimental data on buying decisions, eye-tracking and neurophysiological datasets tied to marketing stimuli, and longitudinal consumer panels. Exclude aggregated national consumption aggregates, firm accounting data without consumer-level linkage, and purely supply-side or production datasets.

research_desc: Datasets that record COVID-19 cases, testing, clinical outcomes, behaviors, mobility, and survey responses during the pandemic.
research_narr: Include case counts, hospitalization and mortality records, seroprevalence studies, testing and vaccination registries, contact-tracing datasets, mobility and social-distancing mobility data, clinical trials on COVID-19 treatments/vaccines, and population surveys about behavior and attitudes toward COVID-19 measures. Exclude datasets unrelated to COVID-19 timing or population (e.g., pre-2019 respiratory virus datasets) unless explicitly connected to COVID-19 analyses.

research_desc: Datasets on political regimes, elections, public opinion, and institutional measures relevant to democracy studies.
research_narr: Include election results, voter turnout data, public-opinion surveys on democratic attitudes (e.g., ESS, WVS), panel studies on political behavior, cross-national indices of democracy and rights (V-Dem, Polity, Freedom House), and expert-coded datasets on institutional features. Exclude datasets that are purely administrative or non-political without connection to democratic processes.

research_desc: Datasets from clinical trials, cohort studies, epidemiological surveys, and registries that measure depression or depressive symptoms.
research_narr: Include datasets containing diagnostic assessments (DSM/ICD), symptom scales (PHQ-9, BDI, CES-D), treatment outcomes, health-care utilization for depression, longitudinal cohort data on mental health, and administrative psychiatric registries. Exclude datasets lacking measures of depressive symptoms or diagnosis, or those focused solely on unrelated psychiatric conditions without depression measures.

research_desc: Datasets measuring internet and technology use, digital skills, platform activity, and indicators of digital infrastructure and adoption.
research_narr: Include surveys on internet use and digital skills (e.g., Eurostat ICT surveys), platform and social-media usage logs, broadband/infrastructure coverage data, administrative data on e-government uptake, digital economy indicators, and user-behavior analytics. Exclude purely technical system-logs with no human behavior component or datasets only about non-digital (analog) processes.

research_desc: Datasets and data collections measuring digital competence or related digital skill indicators.
research_narr: Include survey datasets, assessment results, standardized test data, longitudinal studies and cohort data that contain direct measures of digital skills (objective test scores or validated self-assessments), digital literacy modules within broader surveys, log data tied to skill assessment tasks, and metadata/codebooks. Include national or international assessments (or subcomponents) measuring digital competence and datasets from intervention studies evaluating training programs. Exclude raw technical network logs, purely system-level performance metrics, or usage-only telemetry that cannot be linked to measures of competence or documented assessment tasks.

research_desc: Datasets addressing relationships between digitalization and work: job tasks, employment outcomes, firm ICT use and platform work.
research_narr: Include surveys of firms and workers with measures of ICT adoption, task composition and automation exposure, administrative labor-market data linked to technology indicators, employer-level datasets on digital investments and HR outcomes, job vacancy and skills demand data, longitudinal panels tracking workers through technological change, and platform work datasets (gig economy). Include metadata and codebooks. Exclude datasets that measure only technical network metrics or consumer digital behavior without workplace or labor-market linkages.

research_desc: Workplace-level datasets capturing digital technologies, task changes and worker outcomes.
research_narr: Include firm or establishment surveys with modules on workplace digitization, employee surveys tied to specific workplaces, observational data on task workflows pre/post digital introduction, administrative HR records matched to technology deployment, and longitudinal employer-employee linked data capturing digital transitions. Include metadata and instruments used to collect data. Exclude datasets that record only high-level national ICT indicators without workplace disaggregation.

research_desc: Data collections that enable analysis of digitization effects on employment, occupations and workplaces.
research_narr: Include datasets on technology adoption, occupational task measures, job postings scraped for digital skill demand, employer and employee surveys with digitization modules, longitudinal labor market panels, and matched employer-employee data linking technology use to outcomes. Include structured metadata, codebooks and documentation enabling reproducible analysis. Exclude datasets limited to consumer digital engagement or network performance metrics unrelated to work.

research_desc: Datasets documenting discriminatory patterns and related variables within school settings.
research_narr: Include student-level administrative data on enrollment, tracking, disciplinary actions, assessment results and school placement disaggregated by protected characteristics; school climate surveys with measures of perceived discrimination; teacher referral and evaluation records; longitudinal cohort studies tracking minority student outcomes; and datasets from evaluations of anti-discrimination interventions. Include codebooks and variable documentation. Exclude anonymized datasets lacking any indicators of group membership or any variables enabling analysis of discrimination.

research_desc: Datasets and data collections measuring experiences, perceptions, or instances of discrimination, including survey data, audit studies, administrative records, and experimental datasets.
research_narr: Include datasets that contain variables or modules on perceived discrimination, experienced discriminatory events, audit study outcomes, employer/staffing discrimination experiments, complaints or case records, and indicators of institutional discrimination across domains (employment, education, housing, health). Also include longitudinal and cross-national surveys with discrimination modules. Exclude datasets that do not contain any discrimination-related measures, purely biomedical datasets unrelated to social discrimination, or data that only use 'discrimination' as an unrelated technical term.

research_desc: Datasets on educational processes and outcomes: enrollment, attainment, test scores, longitudinal cohort studies, school census data, administrative records, and program evaluation data.
research_narr: Include survey datasets (e.g., PISA, TIMSS, national education surveys), administrative school records, longitudinal cohorts tracking educational trajectories, datasets from randomized or quasi-experimental evaluations of educational interventions, and labor market datasets that include education variables. Exclude datasets lacking education-related variables or those where education appears only as a minor demographic descriptor without substantive educational measures.

research_desc: Datasets containing measures of attitudes toward Islam or Muslims: survey modules, opinion polls, longitudinal attitude panels, and experimental data on prejudice or intergroup attitudes.
research_narr: Relevant datasets include public opinion surveys and modules with questions about feelings toward Islam/Muslims, trust, perceived threat, support for policies affecting Muslims, and measures of Islamophobia; panel datasets tracking attitude change; and experimental datasets testing interventions to change attitudes. Exclude datasets without items on Islam/Muslim attitudes or those that only record respondents' religious affiliation without attitudinal measures.

research_desc: Datasets with measures of attitudes toward immigration: national and international opinion polls, survey modules on immigration policy preferences, and experimental datasets on migration attitudes.
research_narr: Relevant are surveys containing items on immigration attitudes (e.g., desired levels of immigration, attitudes toward refugees, economic/cultural threat questions), longitudinal panels tracking attitude shifts, and experimental datasets testing interventions or framing effects. Include data that disaggregate attitudes by target group (e.g., refugees, labor migrants). Exclude datasets lacking immigration-attitude measures or those solely documenting migration statistics without attitudinal content.

research_desc: Datasets containing measures of attitudes toward foreigners: opinion polls, social surveys, longitudinal panels, and experiments measuring xenophobia or social distance to non-nationals.
research_narr: Include datasets with items on feelings toward foreigners, willingness to accept foreigners as neighbors/co-workers, perceived threats from foreigners, and policy preferences affecting foreigners. Experimental and vignette datasets that manipulate foreigner characteristics are relevant. Exclude datasets without questions on foreigners or those that treat 'foreigner' only as a trait of respondents without attitudinal measures.

research_desc: Survey datasets, panel data, and experimental data that measure attitudes toward foreigners, immigrants, or ethnic outgroups, including national social surveys, migration modules, and cross-national datasets.
research_narr: Include datasets containing variables measuring attitudes to foreigners/immigrants (e.g., feeling thermometers, social distance, willingness to accept immigrants, perceived threats), experimental vignette data on outgroup attitudes, and modules from large surveys (e.g., ESS, Eurobarometer, World Values Survey, national social surveys) that explicitly ask about 'Fremde' or immigrants. Exclude datasets without attitudinal items about foreigners, purely administrative population registers, and datasets that only record migration flows without public-opinion measures.

research_desc: Datasets containing measures of gender attitudes: survey modules on gender role beliefs, support for gender equality, sexism scales, and related behavioral intention items from national and cross-national surveys.
research_narr: Include datasets with items on gender role ideology, support for gender equality policies (e.g., quotas, parental leave), ambivalent sexism measures, and behavioral measures related to gender attitudes. Relevant sources include ESS, ISSP modules on family and gender, World Values Survey items, national gender surveys, and experimental datasets on gender attitudes. Exclude datasets lacking attitudinal measures about gender or those that only record respondents' gender without opinion items.

research_desc: Datasets that measure attitudes toward Islam or Muslims: national and cross-national opinion surveys, targeted attitude modules, and experimental data on anti-Muslim attitudes and social distance.
research_narr: Include datasets with items on favorability/unfavorability toward Islam or Muslims, perceived threat from Islam (cultural/security), social distance measures vis-à-vis Muslims, support for policies affecting Muslims (e.g., mosque building, headscarf bans), and experimental manipulations about Muslim identity. Relevant sources include ESS, Eurobarometer, World Values Survey, national opinion polls, and specialized Islamophobia studies. Exclude datasets without Islam/Muslim attitudinal measures and administrative datasets with only population counts.

research_desc: Datasets relevant to employment in Poland: national labor force surveys, administrative employment registers, EU microdata (e.g., EU LFS, SILC), and specialized Polish panel studies containing employment variables.
research_narr: Include datasets that provide employment status, occupation, industry, working hours, wages, contract type, transitions in employment, and job search variables for Poland. Examples include the Polish Labour Force Survey, EU-LFS extracts for Poland, Generations and Gender Survey Poland if containing employment modules, and administrative social security/employment registers. Exclude datasets without employment-related variables or those not covering Poland specifically.

research_desc: Datasets containing measures of work alienation or related constructs (job meaning, engagement, burnout, job satisfaction) from workplace surveys, employee panels, and national surveys with work modules.
research_narr: Include datasets with items operationalizing work alienation (e.g., Seeman-based scales), measures of job meaning, autonomy, control, task variety, and social isolation at work. Relevant sources include organizational surveys, European Working Conditions Survey, national workplace panels, and company employee surveys. Exclude datasets that only record occupation or industry without attitudinal/psychological measures concerning work experience.

research_desc: Datasets that measure environmental conditions, exposures, policies or human attitudes/behaviours toward the environment, including monitoring data, survey modules and geospatial/environmental health data.
research_narr: Include datasets containing environmental monitoring (air, water, soil quality), geospatial data on land use/green space, exposure and health linkage data, longitudinal or cross-sectional surveys with environmental modules (attitudes, behaviour, risk perception), and policy or administrative databases on environmental regulation and implementation. Exclude datasets unrelated to environmental phenomena (e.g., purely economic or organizational datasets) unless they contain substantive environmental measures or linkages.

research_desc: Survey and panel datasets that include measures of environmental attitudes and related constructs (e.g., ISSP Environment module, European Social Survey items, national surveys with environmental questions).
research_narr: Include cross-sectional and longitudinal survey datasets, modules and harmonized collections containing items on environmental concern, NEP items, willingness-to-pay, perceived risks, and behavioural intentions. Also include experimental datasets testing interventions to change environmental attitudes. Exclude datasets lacking attitudinal items or containing only objective environmental measures with no attitudinal/perceptual variables.

research_desc: Datasets relevant to Erziehung: household and family surveys, child development panels, school-based studies, and longitudinal cohorts that record parenting, education, and socialization measures.
research_narr: Include datasets with variables on parenting style, parental involvement, child outcomes (cognitive, socioemotional), early childhood programs, educational attainment and pedagogical interventions. Prefer datasets with items or variables labeled in German or from German-speaking contexts, but also include international data relevant to upbringing and education research. Exclude datasets that do not contain measures related to upbringing, parenting or educational processes.

research_desc: Datasets derived from evaluations of social work programs: administrative case files, outcome measurement datasets, longitudinal follow-ups of clients, and monitoring data collected for program assessment.
research_narr: Include datasets from randomized or quasi-experimental evaluations of social work interventions, routine outcome monitoring systems used by social service agencies, administrative records on service delivery and client outcomes, and qualitative evaluation datasets (interviews, focus groups). Prefer datasets containing pre/post measures, comparison groups, or implementation fidelity metrics. Exclude datasets from unrelated social programs unless they are directly relevant to social work services and evaluation.

research_desc: Survey datasets containing measures of external political efficacy: e.g., ANES, ESS, Eurobarometer, ISSP, GSS and national election studies that include efficacy items.
research_narr: Include datasets with one- or multi-item measures of external political efficacy (e.g., items about responsiveness of government, influence over decisions), often alongside political trust and participation measures. Preference for datasets enabling comparative analysis or longitudinal study of efficacy. Exclude datasets lacking efficacy or closely related attitudinal items.

research_desc: Datasets capturing employment and family variables: panel surveys, cross‑sectional household surveys, time‑use studies, administrative employment and benefits records, and matched employer‑employee data.
research_narr: Include datasets that enable analysis of parents' labour force participation, working hours, occupation, leave uptake, childcare utilization, household composition, and related outcomes (income, job mobility). Relevant types: longitudinal panels (e.g., household panels, cohort studies), time‑use diaries, register/administrative data linking employment and family status, employer surveys on flexible work, and cross‑national comparative data. Exclude purely clinical or genomic datasets, datasets without family or employment variables, and those lacking documentation for construction of family/employment indicators.

research_desc: Datasets that document career histories alongside family events: panel studies, employer HR data, administrative registers linking employment, earnings and family status, and qualitative career interview data.
research_narr: Include data enabling analysis of career outcomes in relation to family life: longitudinal employment histories, wage records, promotions, occupational codes, parental leave records, family formation dates, and childcare usage. Relevant sources: national registers, household panels, employer HR databases, and life history interview datasets. Datasets should permit temporal sequencing of family events and career changes. Exclude datasets lacking career trajectory or family event information.

research_desc: Surveys and qualitative datasets that capture gender attitudes, division of household labour, parental involvement, childcare responsibilities, and temporal changes (repeat cross‑sections, panels, time‑use data).
research_narr: Include datasets documenting attitudes toward gender roles (e.g., ESS, WVS), time‑use diaries showing allocation of domestic and care tasks, panel or cohort studies measuring change over time within households, and qualitative interview collections on gendered practices. Also include cross‑national comparative datasets that allow study of policy impacts on gender roles. Exclude datasets that lack measures of gender attitudes or intra‑household task allocation.

research_desc: Comprehensive datasets on family and household topics: censuses, household surveys, panel/cohort studies, vital statistics, register data, time‑use studies, and qualitative family interview collections.
research_narr: Include data sources that allow analysis of family composition and dynamics: national censuses and vital registration (births, marriages, deaths), household budget and labour force surveys with family modules, longitudinal household panels, cohort studies following family life courses, time‑use surveys for household behaviour, and qualitative datasets on family relationships. Data should contain household/kinship identifiers or modules to construct family units. Exclude datasets unrelated to family or lacking documentation to assemble family measures.

research_desc: Datasets linking family composition and behaviour to gendered attitudes and practices: time‑use, attitude surveys, household panels with gender modules, administrative data with parental gender roles, and qualitative gendered family studies.
research_narr: Include datasets providing measures of family structure, division of labour, caregiving, parental leave/use by sex, employment by gender, and gender attitude items. Relevant sources: time‑use surveys disaggregated by sex, cross‑national attitude surveys (ESS, WVS), panel datasets capturing changes in family roles by gender, and qualitative interview sets focused on gendered family experiences. Exclude datasets lacking sex‑disaggregated family measures or gender attitude indicators.

research_desc: Datasets and survey modules that record employment contract and arrangement details: employment status, contract type (permanent/temporary), working hours, self-employment vs. employee, agency/gig work, telework/home-based work, job tenure and multiple job-holding. Typical sources include labor force surveys, panel studies and employer-employee linked data.
research_narr: Relevant data: microdata from labor force surveys and panels (e.g., EU-LFS, national LFS/microcensus, household panel surveys such as SOEP/GSOEP, CPS, national longitudinal employer-employee datasets) and targeted surveys of gig/platform workers or temporary agency workers that contain variables describing contract type, working hours, pay basis, and job security. Include administrative or employer establishment data that can be linked to individual contract types. Exclude datasets that only provide aggregate employment counts without contract-level detail, or data that cover organizational/legal forms unrelated to individual worker contracts.

research_desc: Datasets and study materials measuring leadership constructs and trust outcomes in workplaces, teams or organizations, preferably containing scales for trust in supervisor/management and leadership style/behavior variables.
research_narr: Relevant data: employee surveys, establishment surveys and linked employer–employee datasets with modules on perceived leadership behaviors, leader–member exchange (LMX), and trust in supervisors/management; experimental or longitudinal datasets examining trust-building interventions or changes in leadership. Include German-language datasets or datasets with validated German translations of trust and leadership scales. Exclude datasets that only measure generalized social trust without workplace/leader referent or those that use 'Führung' only in non-leadership contexts.

research_desc: Datasets containing measures of leadership behavior, style, effectiveness, leader-member relations, and leadership development interventions: surveys, 360-degree feedback datasets, organizational case studies and experimental datasets.
research_narr: Relevant data: employee surveys with leadership modules, 360-degree assessment datasets, leadership training evaluation data, longitudinal organizational studies that track leadership and outcomes, and cross-national datasets with leadership items. Include datasets with German-language instruments. Exclude datasets that use 'Führung' in non-leadership senses (e.g., product manuals) or datasets lacking explicit leadership measures.

research_desc: Datasets that include measures of gender-role attitudes or behaviors: national social surveys and modules (e.g., ISSP Family and Changing Gender Roles, European Social Survey, World Values Survey), household surveys with division-of-labor items, and panel studies tracking role attitudes over time.
research_narr: Relevant data: survey modules with items on beliefs about gendered responsibilities (work vs. family), attitudes toward women working, childcare and housework allocation, and measures of gender-role identity (BSRI, role salience). Include datasets that allow analysis by cohort, education and employment. Exclude datasets that only record biological sex without measures of role attitudes or behavior.

research_desc: Datasets containing gender-related variables: surveys with sex and gender identity items, administrative records with gender markers, studies on gender-based outcomes (employment, health, violence), and datasets incorporating non-binary and transgender measures.
research_narr: Relevant data: microdata that record gender identity/expression (including two-step measures: sex at birth and current gender), datasets on gender-based violence, labor-market datasets with gender-disaggregated indicators, and qualitative datasets on gender experience. Include data with non-binary categories or explicit gender modules. Exclude datasets that only capture sex at birth without any conceptualization of gender when the research question concerns gender as identity or social role.

research_desc: Datasets and study collections that contain measures related to gender attitudes, gender identity, gendered behaviours, gender inequality indicators, or qualitative interview/ethnographic data about gender.
research_narr: Include: survey microdata, panel data, census variables with gender breakdowns, datasets of interviews, focus groups or ethnographies on gender, data on gender‑based violence, gender pay gap microdata, and indicator datasets (e.g., gender equality indices). Exclude: datasets that only record biological measures (e.g., hormone levels) without social/gender variables; administrative data with only binary sex codes and no contextual gender variables unless reinterpreted by authors as gendered outcomes.

research_desc: Datasets that contain measures of general self‑efficacy (total scores or item‑level data), including longitudinal and cross‑sectional studies where general self‑efficacy is a variable.
research_narr: Include: survey datasets, cohort studies and experiments that include the General Self‑Efficacy Scale (GSE) or equivalent general self‑efficacy measures, with documentation of items and scoring. Exclude: datasets containing only domain‑specific self‑efficacy measures without a general/self‑efficacy instrument.

research_desc: Datasets that allow analysis of Generation Y, either by explicit cohort identifiers or by birth year ranges enabling cohort selection.
research_narr: Include: survey and panel data with respondent birth year or age so Generation Y can be selected, longitudinal cohorts covering Millennials, and administrative datasets where cohort membership can be inferred. Exclude: datasets lacking age or birth year information or those where cohort analysis is impossible.

research_desc: Datasets containing measures labeled generelle Selbstwirksamkeit or the German version of the General Self‑Efficacy Scale, including item‑level data and scale scores.
research_narr: Include: German surveys, cohort studies, or international datasets with German subsamples that include the Allgemeine Selbstwirksamkeit/GSE items; documentation of translations and reliability statistics. Exclude: datasets with only domain‑specific self‑efficacy items and no general self‑efficacy measure.

research_desc: Datasets containing measures of gender role attitudes, household division of labour, occupational segregation, socialization practices and related qualitative data on gender roles.
research_narr: Include: survey modules (e.g., ISSP family/gender modules, ESS items) with gender role attitude items, time‑use data showing division of labour, interview/ethnographic datasets on role socialization, and administrative data on occupational gender segregation. Exclude: datasets that only record respondent sex without any measures of roles, attitudes or behaviour.

research_desc: Datasets that capture gender role attitudes, behaviors, and role-related practices. Examples: social surveys, time-use studies, cohort studies with role-related modules, cross-national modules on family and gender attitudes.
research_narr: Include datasets containing measures of gender role attitudes or behaviors (e.g. survey items on who should do childcare/housework, occupational role expectations, caregiving roles), time-use data showing division of labor, cohort studies with socialization or role items, and cross-national modules (e.g. ISSP, ESS modules) that permit analysis of gender-role constructs. Exclude datasets that only record biological sex without any measures of roles, datasets about organizational job roles unrelated to gender, or animal/biological datasets.

research_desc: Datasets enabling analysis of gender-role norms and their distribution: repeated surveys, cross-national modules, longitudinal cohorts, and qualitative collections about role expectations.
research_narr: Include datasets with items on gender-role stereotypes, who-does-what behavioral measures, attitudes toward traditional vs. egalitarian roles, and longitudinal data tracking role change. Relevant sources include ISSP modules on family/gender, ESS items, national attitude surveys, time-use surveys, and qualitative interview corpora on gender norms. Exclude datasets that lack role-related content or only record biological sex.

research_desc: Health-related datasets such as health surveys, administrative health records, registries, clinical trial data, population health surveillance and biomarker datasets.
research_narr: Include national health surveys (e.g. GEDA, DEGS, SOEP health modules), disease registries, hospital discharge data, mortality records, cohort studies with health measures, and clinical trial datasets. Data should permit analysis of morbidity, mortality, health behaviors, service use, and biomarkers. Exclude datasets that do not contain health-related variables or that pertain only to non-human subjects unless explicitly relevant.

research_desc: Datasets focused on mental health: psychiatric registries, population mental health surveys, clinical trial data for mental health treatments, and cohort studies with mental health measures.
research_narr: Include datasets containing validated measures of mental disorders or symptoms (diagnoses, symptom scales), service use for mental health, suicide and self-harm registries, and longitudinal cohorts tracking mental health. Examples: national mental health surveys, DRKS/clinical trial datasets for psychiatric interventions, and epidemiological studies with GHQ/PHQ/BDI. Exclude datasets lacking mental health variables or focusing purely on neurological physiology absent psychological measures.

research_desc: Datasets concerning patients: clinical registries, hospital administrative data, electronic health records, patient surveys, and trial participant data.
research_narr: Include datasets with patient-level clinical data (diagnoses, treatments, outcomes), registries for specific diseases, hospital discharge datasets, electronic health record extracts, patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and satisfaction surveys, and randomized controlled trial data with patient participants. Exclude population surveys that do not identify patient status, and datasets that only cover healthy volunteers without patient groups.

research_desc: Datasets and research data on company- or workplace-level health indicators, intervention trials in enterprises, and organizational surveys of health management.
research_narr: Include datasets from workplace health promotion trials, company-level surveys of health policies and OSH practices, administrative records on workplace sickness absence, worksite exposure assessments, aggregated firm-level health outcome data, and longitudinal employer cohorts. Data must be linked to workplace context (e.g., firm, department, occupational group) or evaluate interventions implemented at the company level. Exclude population-level health surveys without workplace identifiers, clinical patient registries not capturing workplace variables, or datasets only about health care utilization outside employment context.

research_desc: Research datasets documenting health outcomes and exposures measured within workplaces or among employed persons.
research_narr: Relevant data include occupational cohort studies, company-level health surveillance data, surveys of working conditions and self-reported health, exposure measurement data gathered on-site, records of work-related incidents, and evaluation datasets of workplace interventions. Datasets should explicitly link health measures to workplace setting or employment status. Exclude datasets limited to non-working populations, general health surveys lacking work-related variables, or clinical trials unrelated to workplace implementation.

research_desc: Individual-level datasets on the health status, health behaviors, and work-related exposures of employed persons.
research_narr: Include worker cohorts, cross-sectional and longitudinal surveys of employed populations, administrative employment-health linkage data, sick-leave registries, occupational disease registries, and biomonitoring data for employed groups. Data should permit analysis of health outcomes among workers. Exclude datasets that do not distinguish employed from non-employed participants or that lack employment-related variables.

research_desc: Datasets containing symptom and complaint measures, health complaint inventories, and survey data on symptom prevalence.
research_narr: Include cross-sectional and longitudinal survey data with symptom checklists, occupational health records recording complaints, symptom diary datasets, psychosomatic symptom inventories, and datasets linking complaints to exposures or outcomes (e.g., absence). Data should allow analysis of prevalence, severity, and correlates of health complaints. Exclude datasets lacking direct symptom measures or those limited to clinical diagnostic tests without symptom information.

research_desc: Datasets on experiences and perpetration of violence, crime statistics, victimization surveys, and program evaluation data.
research_narr: Include national and local victimization surveys, longitudinal cohorts with violence exposure data, administrative records (police, social services, healthcare) related to violent incidents, conflict and war-related datasets, and evaluation datasets of violence prevention programs. Data should measure types of violence, timing, perpetrators, settings, and outcomes. Exclude datasets without explicit measures of violence, or those limited to animal or purely economic crime measures without human violence context.

research_desc: Datasets and surveys that measure violence affecting children and adolescents, including victimization surveys, school-based studies, child protection records, and cohort studies with violence-related variables.
research_narr: Include cross-sectional and longitudinal datasets capturing child/adolescent experiences of physical, sexual, emotional abuse, neglect, bullying, dating violence, exposure to domestic or community violence, or perpetration. Relevant sources: school surveys, child protection and CPS administrative data, cohort studies that include violence modules, and criminological victimization surveys disaggregated by age. Data should allow identification of age groups and contexts of violence. Exclude datasets that only cover adult violence without age breakdown, animal violence datasets, or datasets focused solely on macro-level conflict metrics unless they include youth-specific measures.

research_desc: Cross-national datasets and surveys containing life satisfaction measures suitable for global comparisons (e.g., World Values Survey, Gallup World Poll, European Social Survey).
research_narr: Include large-scale international surveys and datasets that include standardized life satisfaction or subjective well‑being items and allow country-level comparisons or global estimates. Relevant sources: World Values Survey, European Social Survey, Gallup World Poll, OECD Better Life Index data on life satisfaction, ISSP, and Harmonized datasets pooling multiple national surveys. Exclude single-country datasets without cross-national linkage, datasets lacking direct life satisfaction or comparable subjective well‑being items, and opinion polls with poor methodological documentation.

research_desc: Datasets covering health status, health behaviors, healthcare utilization, clinical outcomes, and social determinants collected in surveys, cohorts, administrative registers or health surveillance systems.
research_narr: Include national and international health surveys (e.g., health interview surveys, NHIS, DHS, Eurostat health data), longitudinal cohort studies with health measures, hospital/claims administrative datasets, disease registries, and public health surveillance data. Relevant variables include morbidity, mortality, self-rated health, biomarkers, mental health scales, and healthcare access/utilization. Exclude purely genetic sequence repositories without phenotypic health data and datasets solely focused on non-human health.

research_desc: Datasets and surveys measuring telework prevalence, patterns of working from home, associated outcomes (productivity, well‑being), and employer practices.
research_narr: Include labor force and employer surveys with telework modules, time-use surveys that identify home-based work, longitudinal panels tracking shifts to home office (e.g., COVID-era modules), organizational datasets on remote work policies, and ergonomics/occupational health study data for home workers. Relevant variables include telework frequency, hours worked at home, employer support, equipment provided, productivity/self-reported performance, and home working conditions. Exclude datasets about home ownership or household consumption that do not capture work activities, and retail sales datasets for furniture or office equipment unless linked to remote work research.

research_desc: Datasets and administrative sources capturing migration status, flows, immigrant characteristics, integration indicators, and asylum/refugee records.
research_narr: Include population registers, immigration and naturalization administrative data, household and labor force surveys with migrant identifiers (country of birth, citizenship, year of arrival), refugee and asylum seeker databases, longitudinal migrant cohort studies, and datasets on remittances and migrant networks. Data should allow analysis of migration status, origin/destination, length of stay and integration outcomes. Exclude datasets that only report tourist or short-term travel without migration intent, and non-human migration data.

research_desc: Datasets and data collections containing variables suitable for measuring inequality (income, wealth, consumption, health outcomes, educational attainment, employment), including cross-sectional, panel, survey, administrative, and geo-referenced data.
research_narr: Include datasets that enable calculation or analysis of inequality (microdata on earnings, household surveys, labor force surveys, social statistics, health surveys, census microdata, tax records, longitudinal panels). Also include harmonized cross-national datasets and data on distributional outcomes by social group or geography. Exclude datasets unrelated to distributional analysis (e.g., purely biological or lab experimental data with no social disparity measures), and exclude metadata-only records without accessible data or documentation that allows inequality analysis.

research_desc: Datasets capturing perceptions of information credibility, media trust scales, experiments on trust in information, social media content annotated for trustworthiness, and observational data about information consumption and trust outcomes.
research_narr: Include survey data measuring trust in news, institutions, experts, or specific information items; experimental datasets testing interventions on perceived credibility; annotated corpora identifying trustworthy/untrustworthy content; and behavioral traces linking information exposure to trust indicators. Exclude datasets lacking measures related to information credibility or trust, and purely technical logs without contextual trust measures.

research_desc: Datasets related to information policy and politics: legislative texts, policy databases, records of information access requests, datasets on government transparency, censorship events, and datasets tracking political information campaigns.
research_narr: Include collections of laws and regulations on data/information, datasets documenting FOI requests/responses, indices of press freedom/censorship, corpora of political communication campaigns, and cross-national policy indicators on information governance. Exclude technical datasets on information systems without political or policy metadata and datasets unrelated to governance or political uses of information.

research_desc: Datasets on ICT access and use: household ICT surveys, internet usage logs, broadband coverage maps, digital skills assessments, e‑government service usage, and workplace ICT adoption surveys.
research_narr: Include microdata capturing device ownership, internet connectivity, frequency and purpose of ICT use, digital literacy test scores, administrative records of e-service uptake, and geospatial data on network infrastructure. Exclude raw network traffic captures or engineering telemetry lacking demographic/contextual information needed for social analysis of ICT impacts.

research_desc: Datasets containing measures of interest in politics: public opinion surveys, election studies, panel datasets with political attitudinal modules, and time-series surveys tracking political interest over time.
research_narr: Include surveys and panels that include items on interest in politics, frequency of following political news, attention to public affairs, and associated behaviors (voting, protest, civic activities). Relevant sources include national election studies and cross-national surveys (e.g., ESS, Eurobarometer). Exclude datasets that do not include explicit measures of interest in politics or that measure organizational 'interest' rather than individual attitudinal interest.

research_desc: Datasets and study collections that contain measures of individuals' interest in leadership or aspiration for supervisory roles. Includes employee surveys, longitudinal career panels, student career intention surveys, and experimental datasets with variables on leadership intent.
research_narr: Include datasets with explicit variables measuring leadership interest, leadership career intentions, desire for promotion, or willingness to take supervisory tasks. Accept national or organizational employee surveys, student/graduate follow-ups, and experimental data where leadership choice is an outcome. Exclude datasets that only measure organizational leadership outcomes (performance, style) without a variable capturing personal interest or aspiration to lead.

research_desc: Datasets containing measures of employee motivation, work engagement, intrinsic/extrinsic motivation scales, or related constructs in workplace surveys and organizational studies.
research_narr: Include employer or nationally representative surveys and longitudinal panels with variables on work motivation, engagement (e.g., UWES), or motivation-related antecedents/outcomes (performance, turnover). Include experimental and intervention datasets from organizational contexts. Exclude datasets focused on non-work settings (schools, leisure) or those lacking explicit motivation measures.

research_desc: Datasets and surveys containing job satisfaction measures such as overall satisfaction and facet-specific items from employee surveys, national labor studies, and longitudinal panels.
research_narr: Include employer surveys, national labor force panels, organizational climate studies and longitudinal data with validated job satisfaction items (e.g., single-item overall satisfaction, MSQ, JDI). Exclude datasets without job satisfaction measures or those limited to non-work contexts.

research_desc: Datasets and survey collections focused on adolescents: school-based surveys, youth cohorts, health surveillance (e.g., HBSC, national youth health studies), and longitudinal panels tracking adolescent development.
research_narr: Include datasets with adolescent samples or age-disaggregated data covering behaviors, health, education, and social variables. Accept cross-sectional and longitudinal studies, school surveys, and administrative data on youth. Exclude datasets without adolescent-specific data or that aggregate adolescents into broader age ranges without separate indicators.

research_desc: Datasets and studies that collect data on children and/or adolescents: birth cohorts, child health surveys, school-based datasets, family panels, and longitudinal studies that follow minors over time.
research_narr: Include datasets with samples of children and/or adolescents, covering health, development, education and family contexts (e.g., national child health surveys, birth cohort studies). Prefer data with age-specific measures and longitudinal follow-up. Exclude datasets that do not include minors or that only provide adult retrospective reports without direct child/adolescent measures.

research_desc: Datasets and data collections about climate: instrumental temperature and precipitation records, remote sensing/climate model outputs, greenhouse gas inventories, climate indices, observational networks, socio-environmental datasets on climate impacts and perceptions.
research_narr: Relevant data are time series of meteorological variables, gridded climate model outputs (CMIP etc.), satellite-derived climate products, national emissions inventories, and survey datasets on public attitudes toward climate. Include processed and raw data used to analyze climate patterns, impacts or policy outcomes. Exclude datasets unrelated to atmospheric or socio-environmental climate (e.g., 'organizational climate' survey data) unless clearly tied to environmental/climatic topics.

research_desc: Datasets on climate change: observed warming datasets, long-term temperature records, greenhouse gas inventories, emission scenario data, climate model simulations (projections), impact datasets, and survey data on climate change beliefs and behaviors.
research_narr: Include datasets used to quantify historical climate change, future scenario projections (RCP/SSP outputs), national/subnational emission inventories, impact assessments (e.g., crop yields under warming scenarios), and social survey datasets measuring awareness, beliefs, and mitigation/adaptation behaviors. Exclude datasets not directly addressing climate change processes or responses.

research_desc: Datasets about cultural phenomena: cultural participation surveys, heritage inventories, arts statistics, ethnographic corpora, cultural consumption and production datasets, and cross-national value surveys related to culture.
research_narr: Include survey data on cultural participation, attendance, values and identities (e.g., Eurobarometer cultural modules, ESS cultural items), cultural economics data (ticket sales, funding), museum and heritage registries, and coded qualitative corpora on cultural practices. Exclude biomedical culture data (laboratory cell cultures) and datasets that only mention 'culture' metaphorically (organizational climate) without cultural content.

research_desc: Datasets on workplace learning and training: employer-provided training surveys, continuing vocational education statistics, longitudinal employer-employee matched data, apprenticeship records, and surveys on informal learning at work.
research_narr: Include representative surveys of training participation (e.g., CVTS), employer training modules, administrative apprenticeship data, panel data linking training to outcomes (wages, mobility), and qualitative datasets documenting workplace learning practices. Exclude datasets focused on school-based learning without workplace component or datasets about machine learning systems.

research_desc: Datasets containing measures of left-right orientation: national and cross-national survey data with ideological self-placement items (e.g., ESS, ISSP, Eurobarometer), panel studies tracking ideological change, and datasets with party position mappings on left-right scales.
research_narr: Include survey datasets with explicit left-right self-placement or derived ideological scales, manifesto/party placement datasets (e.g., MARPOR), and longitudinal data capturing shifts in ideological identification. Exclude datasets that record only spatial or physical left/right measures or those lacking political ideological indicators.

research_desc: Datasets and data collections containing media content, media usage metrics, social media corpora, audience surveys, content analysis datasets, and platform analytics relevant to media research.
research_narr: Include datasets that record media consumption (time use or audience ratings), survey data on media habits and attitudes, corpora of news articles or social media posts (tweets, Facebook posts, forum threads), annotated content analysis datasets, logs from media platforms, network data about information diffusion, and experimental datasets measuring media effects. Data may be cross-sectional, longitudinal, or event-based and should directly measure media phenomena. Exclude datasets unrelated to communication (e.g., biological media), datasets that only incidentally mention media without measures of media content or use, and raw hardware-level telemetry unrelated to content or audience behavior.

research_desc: Datasets measuring job and work characteristics: surveys, employer records, time-use data, job-exposure matrices, and occupation-level descriptors capturing working conditions and job attributes.
research_narr: Include datasets that contain variables on job content (tasks, complexity), working hours, contract type, autonomy and control, mental/physical demands, ergonomic and safety conditions, pay and benefits, training opportunities, and occupational classifications (ISCO, O*NET type descriptors). Also include longitudinal employer-employee matched data and workplace assessments. Exclude datasets that mention 'work' only as employment status without characteristics, or data solely about company-level outcomes without information on job-level features.

research_desc: Datasets on migration: population registers, survey data on migrants, border statistics, asylum and refugee records, remittance datasets, and mobility histories relevant to migration research.
research_narr: Include data documenting migration flows (origin-destination matrices), migrant stocks, individual-level surveys with migration histories, administrative records on permits and asylum cases, labor migration statistics, longitudinal studies of migrants, remittance transactions, and geocoded mobility data. Datasets should enable analysis of causes, experiences, integration outcomes, or policy impacts of migration. Exclude biological or ecological datasets referring to organismal migration, and datasets that only tangentially mention migration without usable migration measures.

research_desc: Datasets on employees: employer-employee linked datasets, staff surveys, payroll/HR administrative records, occupational panels, and personnel files useful for analyzing employee outcomes and workplace processes.
research_narr: Include datasets that provide individual-level and job-level information on employees such as demographic characteristics, employment contract, tenure, wages, working hours, performance evaluations, training records, absenteeism, and survey measures of well-being and engagement. Also include matched employer-employee datasets and workplace-level contextual variables. Exclude datasets that only cover employers or organizational finances without staff-level information, or lists of collaborators not indicating employment relationships.

research_desc: Datasets on mobility: travel surveys, GPS and smartphone mobility traces, public transport usage, commuting statistics, origin-destination matrices, and longitudinal data on social mobility.
research_narr: Include datasets capturing individual or aggregate movement (travel diaries, sensor/GPS logs, mobile network data, smartcard transit records), commuting flows, modal shares, accessibility measures, transport network attributes, and data on social mobility (intergenerational income/occupation mobility). Also include datasets suited for modeling mobility patterns and evaluating mobility policies. Exclude sensor datasets measuring non-human particle mobility or datasets that do not contain movement or mobility-relevant variables.

research_desc: Datasets collected from employees or workplaces measuring motivational constructs, engagement, job attitudes, or intervention outcomes.
research_narr: Include survey datasets, longitudinal HR panels, intervention trial data, employee engagement indexes, organizational climate surveys and anonymized administrative HR data that contain measures of motivation, job satisfaction, turnover intention, rewards, or performance linked to motivational variables. Include metadata specifying sample, measurement instruments, and scales. Exclude datasets from non-work contexts, small lab samples of non-employee participants, or datasets lacking any measure of motivation or workplace-related outcomes.

research_desc: Datasets that link motivational measures with learning outcomes, instructional variables, or longitudinal learning trajectories.
research_narr: Include datasets from schools, universities, MOOCs, training programs, or experimental studies that contain measures of motivation (e.g., intrinsic/extrinsic scales, goal orientation), study strategies, and objective or self-reported learning outcomes (grades, test scores, skill acquisition). Include learning analytics logs that capture engagement correlated with motivational indicators. Exclude datasets without any motivation-related measures or those purely about cognitive ability without learning motivation content.

research_desc: Datasets measuring both interest and motivational constructs, including their development over time or in response to interventions.
research_narr: Include surveys, longitudinal panels, experimental datasets, and classroom or domain-specific studies that contain measures of situational and personal interest alongside motivation measures and related outcomes (engagement, persistence). Include metadata describing scales and timing. Exclude datasets that measure only one of the constructs (interest or motivation) without linking them, or that treat interest only as demographic/consumption data.

research_desc: Datasets documenting media usage: surveys, time-use diaries, digital trace data, platform analytics, and content consumption logs.
research_narr: Include representative surveys of media habits, longitudinal time-use studies, smartphone/app usage logs, social media activity datasets, web browsing histories (anonymized), and combined self-report and objective measurement datasets that capture platform, frequency, duration, device, and purpose. Include metadata on sampling and measurement methods. Exclude datasets that do not contain media use variables or that only document technical network metrics without user behavior data.

research_desc: Datasets related to online sport and fitness: user logs from fitness apps/platforms, e-sports performance data, intervention trials of online exercise programs, and participation metrics.
